# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 software and engineering firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| remote_share | Share of engineering staff working mostly remote, 2021-2022 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2023 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2023 |
| log_engineers_2020 | Log number of engineers, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2020 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2020, standardized |
| collab_index_2023 | Internal collaboration index from 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| segment | Sector: hardware / software |
| vc_backed | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| founder_ceo | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| cloud_spend_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| hq_in_hub_city | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_phd_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| gross_margin_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of remote work on engineering innovation?

Approach: OLS of patents_per_100_eng_2023 on remote_share with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size, firm age, the pre-period value of the outcome and collab_index_2023, which captures an important determinant of the outcome, and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on remote_share is -2.731 (SE 0.220, p = 0.0000, N = 1960).

Conclusion: negative effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

import pandas as pd, statsmodels.formula.api as smf
d=pd.read_csv('data.csv')
y='patents_per_100_eng_2023'
pre='log_engineers_2020+firm_age_2020+patents_per_100_eng_2020'
pre2=pre+'+vc_backed+founder_ceo+cloud_spend_2020+hq_in_hub_city+share_phd_2020+gross_margin_2020+C(region)+listed+C(segment)'
for f in [y+'~remote_share',y+'~remote_share+'+pre,y+'~remote_share+'+pre2,y+'~remote_share+'+pre+'+collab_index_2023','collab_index_2023~remote_share+'+pre]:
    m=smf.ols(f,d).fit(cov_type='HC1');print(f[-40:],m.params['remote_share'],m.bse['remote_share'])
print(d[['remote_share','collab_index_2023',y]].corr())
E
python3 r.py

content.text:
I rejected the report. I wrote `verdict.json` with that decision.

The report's "negative effect" conclusion depends on one control: `collab_index_2023`. That variable is measured in 2023, after the remote-work period. It is also affected by remote share (coefficient about 0.6 when regressed on remote share and the pre-period controls) and it drives patents. Controlling for it biases the estimate.

I re-ran the regression with different control sets, all with robust standard errors:

| Controls | Remote-share coefficient | SE |
|---|---|---|
| None | +1.60 | 0.24 |
| Pre-period only (firm size, age, 2020 patents) | -0.28 | 0.24 |
| Pre-period plus the other 2020 firm characteristics, region, listing and segment | -0.28 | 0.24 |
| Pre-period plus `collab_index_2023` (the analyst's choice) | -2.91 | 0.23 |

With only pre-period controls the effect is about -0.28 with a standard error of 0.24, so it is not distinguishable from zero. The -2.7 in the report appears only once the 2023 collaboration index is added. The unadjusted +1.60 is also not a clean estimate, because it ignores the pre-period controls.

My -2.91 differs slightly from the report's -2.73 because I did not trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome. I did not re-run the trimmed version, so I haven't checked it.
